chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, raising it, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Every innovation is a straying, and every straying, its way is to the Fire.

key_terms.بِدْعَةٌ: bid'ah — religious innovation, any newly invented religious practice not sanctioned by the Quran or Sunnah
key_terms.ضَلَالَةٌ: dalala — misguidance, straying from the straight path

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq say about religious innovation (bid'ah)?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from both Imam al-Baqir (5th Imam) and Imam al-Sadiq (6th Imam), delivers one of the most well-known warnings in Islamic tradition against religious innovation (bid'ah). The statement condemns any newly invented religious practice that has no basis in the established religion, declaring that it constitutes misguidance and ultimately leads to hellfire. In the context of early Islamic sectarian disputes and the emergence of various theological schools, this warning carried profound weight for believers seeking to preserve authentic religious practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said: ‘
Every innovation is a straying, and every straying, its way is to the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan in a marfu‘ manner (rafa’ahu) from abu Ja’far and abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who have said the following. “
All innovations are misguidance and all misguidance leads to Hell.”
